story: Harrison Ford: “Stop Giving Power to People Who Don't Believe in Science”
text: I don't think we can change the fact that people generally listen to what actors (and other charismatic people) have to say. This is nothing new. For a local example, San Francisco's John Reber, and the plan he pushed to turn the Bay into a freshwater lake ( [VIDEO] is a good video to watch). For a state (California) example, there's Arnold Schwarzenegger. For a national (US-level) example, there's Ronald Reagan. For what it's worth, Harrison Ford seems to be a stand-up guy. For example, his reaction when he accidentally landed his private plane on an airport taxiway: [LINK] So, rather than saying "Stop listening to <insert charismatic group here>", it's better to engage with and educate them.

story: The New Europe With Lasting Peace (100 year old map)
text: > It’s reminiscent of the plan suggested by a school teacher, to dam the San Francisco Bay, which was taken seriously enough to be modeled to scale by the military. For those unaware, I learned of this plan via this short Tom Scott video. Fascinating. [VIDEO] (4:33)

Yeaaaah, like that wouldn't have any unintended consequences. Meanwhile, I find this more interesting: [LINK] The Army Corps of Engineers literally built a scale model of the San Francisco Bay Area, and they used it to figure out that damming the SF Bay was a very, very bad idea: [VIDEO]
